To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the vast majority of ERP transactions are analytical in nature and (ii) it is possible to serve OLTP and OLTP workloads out of the same database.
the combination of columnar data storage and combined columns enables us to process OLAP and OLTP transactions in the same database with high throughput and low latency.
the combination of columnar and combined columnar storage, as well as the use of a single in-memory database system, is a promising approach for processing both ERP transactions and analytics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a new database system for enterprise workloads.
the design of database systems that are able to serve the needs of the modern digital enterprise.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SanssouciDB is an excellent example of how the database community can contribute to the digital transformation of enterprises.
the combination of OLTP and OLTP is possible and can be very beneficial for the user.
we have a system which has a very high throughput for a large number of OLAP queries, but which also has a very good performance for a large number (and a high percentage of) OLTP transactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have built an in-memory columnstore database that is able to process ERP workloads at high speed.
the columnstore technology has been successfully adapted to support OLAP and OLTP in one system.

SanssouciDB can be used for OLTP and OLTP+OLAP workloads with the following benefits: (i) OLTP performance is similar to a traditional database, (ii) OLTP performance can be increased by up to 2x when OLTP and OLAp workloads run together in a single database, and (iii) OLAP performance is increased by up to a factor of 20 compared to a traditional database.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same data store can serve both, OLAP and OLTP workloads.
a database system designed to process both OLAP and OLTP workloads on a single data store can be orders of magnitude faster than a traditional OLAP database system.
it is feasible to combine OLAP and OLTP in the same system, even for large-scale enterprise workloads.
